title: Agent Card carrying an ES256 signature that verifies against a published JWKS
rationale: One known-conforming document serves all three MUST-level signature checks, because they are three stages of one act: resolve the key, verify the signature, and confirm the algorithm was capable of carrying evidence. It is also the only fixture in the pack that proves the instrument agrees with an independent JOSE implementation about what a valid A2A signature is, rather than merely with itself. The pilot found one signed card in twenty-five, so a single false negative here would be a large fraction of the positive class.
key_provenance: The key pair was generated once with joserfc (P-256) and the signature computed over `signing_payload(card)` -- the card without `signatures`, canonicalised per RFC 8785. Only the public half is recorded, which is all a reviewer needs: any JOSE implementation can recompute the JCS payload from the `card` object below and check this signature against `jwks`. Editing the card without re-signing therefore breaks the fixture, which is the intended behaviour for a frozen conformance case.

spec.source: A2A v1.0.1, OUTSIDE the revision decision rule R7 pins
spec.quote: the Agent Card content MUST be canonicalized using the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) as defined in RFC 8785
spec.verification: RESOLVED 5 August 2026, and the answer is that the anchor does not exist. Earlier rounds recorded that A2A 8.4 'could not be retrieved'; it could not be retrieved because A2A v0.3.0 -- the revision decision rule R7 pins -- has no 8.4, no 4.4.7, no reference to RFC 8785, and no RFC 2119 keyword anywhere about card signatures. AgentCardSignature is 5.5.6 and defines a data structure. Those sections exist in v1.0, which R7 does not admit. C03 and C04 are therefore descriptive-only and this fixture pins a recorded observation, not a conviction.
